strategy.angle: Infrastructure bottlenecks as the ultimate barrier to Houston’s AI scaling
strategy.audience: Houston business leaders, CEOs, and CTOs

draft.hook: The greatest threat to your AI strategy isn't your model choice; it is the physical speed at which your data travels between chips.
draft.body: NVIDIA and Coherent Corp just locked a partnership to redefine optical interconnects, proving that the future of enterprise AI isn’t just about more GPUs—it’s about how fast those GPUs can actually talk to each other. In Houston, where we manage massive data loads across energy and logistics sectors, electrical bandwidth is rapidly becoming a lethal performance ceiling. We are approaching a 10x multiplier in data density requirements. Why does this matter for your bottom line? Because data center latency is directly proportional to your operational agility. When I talk to leadership teams at Amplify Intelligence, I emphasize that you aren't just building IT infrastructure; you are building the nervous system of your company. If your data throughput is lagging by even 15% compared to the competition, your predictive analytics will always be a step behind real-time reality.
draft.closing: The winners in the next phase of Houston's industrial AI shift will be the ones who solve the hardware bottleneck before their legacy systems buckle under the sheer weight of their own intelligence.
draft.cta: Look at your current infrastructure roadmap: are you investing in compute power at the expense of total system throughput?
